subject: Dedicated capacity stress-scan & sample workload rundown
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@clearmotive.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity — quick stressor scan and sample payloads

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this — we want to validate latency & concurrency claims before we commit to a Dedicated contract. I attached a small sample of live payloads (anonymized) and a CSV with prompt/response length distribution. High-level ask: could Redwood run a short stressor scan against a representative 1k-request batch so we can see 95th/99th p99 and per-token costs for our observed distribution?

A couple of constraints:
- 90% of our requests are short Q&A (prompt ~40 tokens, reply ~120 tokens), 10% are long summarization (prompt ~800 tokens, reply ~1,600 tokens).
- Typical burst concurrency we expect is 180–250 concurrent requests; steady-state concurrency around 40–60.
- We need a read on whether a single Dedicated pool (4xA100-style) can meet a 200ms p95 for short Q&A and an SLA-friendly p99 for long jobs during normal load.

Attached: sample_payloads_2028q3.jsonl, prompt_length_distribution.csv

We can make a quick workspace available for the run if you prefer. Let us know what you need to get started (tooling access, test tokens, timeline).

—Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Engineering, Clearmotive AI
alex.gomez@clearmotive.ai
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@clearmotive.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-15T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick stressor scan and sample payloads

Alex — thanks for the detail and the example files. We can absolutely run a short stressor scan and surface p95/p99, throughput, and per-token cost estimates. To make the results meaningful, a few clarifying questions: 

1) Distribution timing: is the 180–250 burst expected to last seconds, minutes, or sustained for tens of minutes?
2) Do you have a hard latency SLO (e.g., p95 <200ms for short Q&A) you want us to validate against, or is the 200ms target just a wish/starting point?
3) Are long summarization jobs tolerant of batching (we can queue for micro-batch to reduce cost) or must they be processed with low additional queuing latency?

I'll loop in Ben and Dev for kernel/quantization and batch sizing recommendations. Proposed next steps:
- Internal pre-check (Ben/Dev): map the sample distribution to estimated GPU footprints and a few candidate cluster configs.
- Redwood stressor run (48–72h window): we can simulate both burst and steady patterns; we'll share an initial report and a recommended Dedicated pool sizing and expected unit costs.

If you can confirm (1) burst duration and (2) whether you allow batching for long jobs, we'll schedule the scan for tomorrow morning (PST).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-15T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick stressor scan and sample payloads

Jasmine / Dev — quick notes from a kernel/throughput perspective after a preliminary look at the JSONL:

- Short Q&A (40/120) maps to ~single-token regen loops of ~160 tokens per request; very batch-friendly up to batch=32 on Ampere-class GPUs with quantization.
- Long summaries (800/1600) are KV-cache heavy; they drive memory pressure and favor larger-memory SKUs or model variants with reduced headcount.
- If Clearmotive allows micro-batching of long jobs (batch 2–4 with an upper latency tolerance of ~1s), we can cut per-token cost ~30% while keeping p95 within SLO for short Q&A.

Sizing hypothesis (very rough, needs a stress run):
- 2xA100-80GB (or comparable) nodes for a 24/7 pool to handle steady-state concurrency (60 concurrent short Q&A) with room for background summarization.
- Add a 2-node burst pool (on-demand) to absorb 180–250 spikes; autoscale target to bring total to 4 nodes during bursts.
- Expected p95 for short Q&A in this config: 120–210ms depending on batching aggressiveness and tokenization variance; p99 will depend on tail queuing under burst but should be manageable with autoscale + request prioritization.

I'll prepare a short runbook and a script to replay their JSONL distribution for the stressor. Dev — can you confirm the replay harness and whether we should use prefix caching for the short Q&A traffic?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@clearmotive.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-17T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick stressor scan and sample payloads

Alex — quick update and proposed mutual action plan after our internal sync (Ben + Dev):

1) Immediate ask from your side: confirm expected burst duration (seconds / ~1–5 minutes / >5 minutes) and whether long summarization jobs can tolerate batching up to ~1s additional latency.
2) Redwood will:
   - Run a 4-hour replay tomorrow (PST) that includes a 10-minute burst window at your specified concurrency and a 3-hour steady-state run.
   - Produce a short report: p50/p95/p99 latency for short vs long classes, GPU utilization, cost-per-1k-requests, and recommended Dedicated pool (nodes + burst sizing).
   - Share an SLA-draft tailored to the sizing (attached SLA-draft-CLM4829.pdf) and a cost estimate.
3) Please provide: test tokens (or a temporary workspace link), and confirm permission to run the replay against Redwood dev pool (non-production instance).

We can kick the replay as soon as we have your answers to (1) and (3).

Thanks — looking forward to the results.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
